original: Rhinoplasty reshapes the bone and cartilage of the nose – to change its size or shape, to correct an asymmetry or, where needed, to improve breathing. The plan is made together with your surgeon. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
Usually general anaesthesia
About 2–4 hours
Usually 1 night
Nasal splint
Removed after 5–7 days
You would like to change the shape or size of your nose.
You have breathing problems, for example because of a deviated septum.
The growth of your face is complete.
You are in good general health and do not smoke, or are ready to stop for the surgery.
Types of rhinoplasty
Cosmetic rhinoplasty
Changes the size, tip or nostrils, or corrects an asymmetry.
Functional rhinoplasty
Septorhinoplasty improves breathing, for example with a deviated septum.
Consultation before surgery
The surgeon examines your facial structure, discusses your wishes and makes a personal surgical plan.
Anaesthesia and preparation
You receive general anaesthesia or local anaesthesia with sedation. The area is prepared and precise markings guide the reshaping.
Reshaping the nose
Through small incisions inside the nostrils or at the base of the nose, the surgeon reshapes bone and cartilage – shape, size and symmetry – and corrects breathing problems where needed.
The incisions are closed carefully and a splint supports the new shape. You are monitored closely and receive a personal aftercare plan.
After a pre-operative examination, the operation takes place as planned. You usually stay in hospital for one night.
First week
Bruising and swelling around the eyes usually go down within 7–10 days. The splint is removed after 5–7 days.
First month
Most of the swelling goes down. Avoid strenuous activity and follow the care instructions of your surgeon.
Months 6–12
The tissues settle slowly; the final shape of the nose usually shows after 6–12 months.
Usually 2–4 hours under general anaesthesia, followed by about one night in hospital.
Is it painful?

Modern techniques such as ultrasonic (piezo) surgery are used. Discomfort after the operation is usually mild and is treated with medication; swelling and bruising around the eyes usually go down within 7–10 days.
When is the splint removed?
The surgeon removes the splint and any nasal packing after about 5–7 days.
When will I see the final result?
Most swelling goes down within the first month; the final, detailed shape usually shows after 6–12 months.
Plan your rhinoplasty

A mommy makeover combines several procedures in one operation to address changes after pregnancy and childbirth – for example loose skin and separated abdominal muscles, a change in breast shape or stubborn fat deposits. Which procedures are combined is decided together with your surgeon. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
Usually 1–2 nights
After about 2–4 weeks
Final result
After 6–12 months
You have completed your family planning and are no longer breastfeeding.
You would like to address several changes after pregnancy at the same time.
What it can include
Removes excess skin and tightens the abdominal muscles.
Restores the shape and volume of the breasts.
Removes stubborn fat on the abdomen, hips or thighs.
For example labiaplasty, if you wish.
Consultation with the surgeon
Before the operation, the surgeon examines you in person, discusses your wishes and confirms the final plan – which procedures are combined.
On the day of surgery you receive general anaesthesia and sleep throughout the operation. The team marks and prepares the areas to be treated.
The combined procedures
The planned procedures – for example a tummy tuck, breast surgery and liposuction – are performed in one session. The duration depends on the combination.
Closure and first care
The incisions are closed carefully and dressed. You are closely monitored in the first hours and usually stay in hospital for 1–2 nights.
The surgeon recommends which procedures to combine. We plan your dates, flights, hotel and transfers around it.
After a pre-operative examination, the operation takes place under general anaesthesia. You usually stay in hospital for 1–2 nights.
Gentle movement soon after surgery and 1–2 nights in hospital. Follow the care instructions of your surgeon.
Weeks 2–4
Most people gradually return to their daily activities. Heavy lifting and sport come later, as advised.
Swelling goes down over the weeks; the final result usually shows after 6–12 months.
Which procedures are combined?
This is planned individually. A mommy makeover often combines a tummy tuck, a breast lift or augmentation and liposuction – depending on your body and your wishes.
Can I get pregnant after a mommy makeover?
Yes, but a later pregnancy can stretch the skin and abdominal muscles again and change the result. For this reason it is usually recommended to wait until your family planning is complete.
How long is the recovery?
It depends on the combination of procedures. Most people return to their daily activities after about 2–4 weeks; heavy lifting and sport take longer.
This is planned individually with the clinic, depending on the procedures. We organise your flights and hotel accordingly.
Plan your mommy makeover

A tummy tuck removes excess skin and fat from the abdomen and tightens the underlying muscles – often after major weight loss or pregnancy. Whether a full or a mini abdominoplasty suits you is decided with your surgeon. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
After about 10–14 days
You have loose abdominal skin or weakened abdominal muscles after weight loss or pregnancy.
Ideally, your family planning is complete.
Types of tummy tuck
Full abdominoplasty
An incision from hip to hip, often with repositioning of the navel.
Mini abdominoplasty
A shorter incision for minor excess skin below the navel.
The surgeon examines your abdomen, discusses your wishes and plans how excess skin, fat and weakened muscles are treated.
You receive general anaesthesia. The area is prepared and marked to guide the skin and muscle adjustments.
Removing excess skin and fat
Through a horizontal incision in the lower abdomen, the surgeon removes excess skin and fat and tightens the abdominal muscles. Liposuction is sometimes combined.
The incision is closed with fine sutures and a compression garment is put on. You usually stay in hospital for 1–2 nights.
After a pre-operative examination, the operation takes place as planned. You usually stay in hospital for 1–2 nights.
Gentle walking soon after surgery and 1–2 nights in hospital. A compression garment supports healing.
Weeks 2–6
Most people return to work and light routines after 10–14 days. The compression garment is worn for 4–6 weeks.
After 6 weeks
Heavy lifting and strenuous sport are possible again, as advised by your surgeon.
About 2–4 hours under general anaesthesia, depending on whether a full or mini tummy tuck is done, followed by 1–2 nights in hospital.
Do I need to wear a compression garment?
Yes, usually for 4–6 weeks. It reduces swelling and supports the new contour.
When can I return to work?
Most people return to work and light routines after 10–14 days; heavy lifting should wait about 6 weeks.
Can I get pregnant after a tummy tuck?
Yes, but a later pregnancy can stretch the skin and muscles again. It is usually recommended to wait until your family planning is complete.
Plan your tummy tuck

Breast augmentation increases the size and volume of the breasts or restores volume lost after weight changes or pregnancy – with implants or with your own fat. Implant type, size and incision site are chosen with your surgeon. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
About 1.5–2 hours
After about 5–7 days
You would like more breast volume or a different shape.
You would like to restore volume after weight changes or pregnancy.
Your breasts are noticeably uneven.
What can be chosen
Silicone or saline implants
Different shapes and sizes, chosen to suit your body.
Your own fat
Fat transfer: your own fat is moved to the breasts.
Incision site
Under the breast, around the areola or in the armpit.
After a detailed consultation about your wishes and your health, the operation takes place under general anaesthesia.
Incision and implant placement
A small incision is made under the breast, around the areola or in the armpit, and the implant is placed for the planned size and shape.
Shaping and symmetry
The surgeon shapes the breasts and adjusts the position of the implants – or the distribution of transferred fat – to your proportions.
The incisions are closed with fine sutures and you are monitored in the recovery area. You usually stay in hospital for one night.
Walking is possible within hours. A supportive bra helps healing and reduces swelling.
Week 1
Most people return to work and light routines after about 5–7 days.
Weeks 4–6
The supportive bra is worn for about 4–6 weeks; sport and heavy lifting come later, as advised.
Which implants are used?
Modern cohesive silicone gel implants or saline implants; fat transfer is also possible. The surgeon explains the options – type, shape and size – in your consultation.
About 1.5–2 hours under general anaesthesia, usually with one night in hospital.
Most people return to light routines after about 5–7 days.
How long do I wear a special bra?
Usually for about 4–6 weeks, to support healing.
Plan your breast augmentation

Liposuction removes stubborn fat deposits that do not respond to diet and exercise, for example on the abdomen, waist, thighs, arms or neck, to shape the body contour. It is not a method for losing weight. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
Local with sedation or general
Same day or 1 night
Compression garment
For about 4–6 weeks
After 3–6 months
You have local fat deposits that do not respond to diet and exercise.
Your weight is stable and close to your goal weight.
You understand that liposuction shapes the body but is not a weight-loss treatment.
Common treatment areas
Abdomen and waist
Including the flanks for a smoother waistline.
Thighs
Inner and outer thighs.
Arms, back and chest
Upper arms, the back and – for men – the chest.
Neck and chin
For a more defined jawline.
The surgeon assesses the areas to be treated, discusses your wishes and makes a personal treatment plan.
Depending on the area and extent, you receive local anaesthesia with sedation or general anaesthesia. The areas are marked and prepared.
Fat removal and contouring
Through small incisions, a thin cannula loosens and removes the fat – depending on the plan also with Vaser or laser-assisted techniques – and the area is shaped evenly.
The small incisions are closed and a compression garment is put on. Depending on the extent, you go home the same day or after one night.
After a pre-operative examination, the operation takes place as planned. Depending on the extent, you go to your hotel the same day or after one night in hospital.
Walking is possible within hours. The compression garment reduces swelling.
Weeks 3–6
First changes in shape usually show after 3–4 weeks. The garment is worn for 4–6 weeks.
Months 3–6
Once the swelling has gone, the final result usually shows after 3–6 months.
Is liposuction a way to lose weight?
No. It removes local fat deposits to shape the body; it does not replace a healthy weight.
Is the result permanent?
The removed fat cells do not come back, but a stable weight with a healthy lifestyle is needed to keep the result.
How long do I wear the compression garment?
Usually for 4–6 weeks, to control swelling and help the skin adapt.
When will I see the result?
First changes usually after 3–4 weeks; the final result after 3–6 months, once the swelling has gone.
Plan your liposuction

Gynecomastia surgery (male breast reduction) removes excess glandular tissue and fat for a flatter chest – with liposuction, direct removal of tissue or both. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
General or local anaesthesia
About 1–2 hours
For about 3–4 weeks
You have enlarged breast tissue, for example due to hormones, genetics, weight changes or medication.
The cause has been checked by a doctor.
Techniques
Removes excess fat through small incisions.
Tissue removal
Removes firm glandular tissue directly.
Combination
Both techniques together, if needed.
After a detailed consultation about your wishes and your health, the operation takes place under general or local anaesthesia.
Liposuction and tissue removal
Excess fat is removed by liposuction; where needed, glandular tissue and excess skin are removed directly.
Contouring the chest
If a lot of tissue is removed, the nipples may be repositioned. The chest is shaped evenly on both sides.
The incisions are closed and a compression vest is put on. You go home the same day or after one night.
After a pre-operative examination, the operation takes place as planned. You go to your hotel the same day or after one night in hospital.
Weeks 3–4
The compression garment is worn for about 3–4 weeks.
Later
Sport and heavy lifting come back step by step, as advised by your surgeon.
About 1–2 hours under general or local anaesthesia, usually as a day case or with one night in hospital.
Do I need a compression garment?
Yes, usually for about 3–4 weeks, to reduce swelling and support the new chest contour.
Where are the incisions?
Along the edge of the areola or in natural folds, so that the scars are as inconspicuous as possible.
Plan your gynecomastia surgery

A breast lift raises and reshapes sagging breasts – for example after pregnancy, breastfeeding, weight changes or with age – by removing excess skin, tightening the surrounding tissue and placing the nipple higher. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
About 2–3 hours
After about 7–10 days
Your breasts have lost firmness or sit lower after pregnancy, breastfeeding or weight changes.
Breast lift
Raises and reshapes the breasts with your own tissue.
Lift with implants
If volume is also lost, silicone implants can be placed in the same operation.
Incision and reshaping
Through precisely placed incisions, excess skin is removed and the breast tissue is lifted and reshaped.
Nipple position and symmetry
The nipple is moved to a higher position and any asymmetry is corrected.
The incisions are closed with fine sutures and a supportive bra is put on. You usually stay in hospital for one night.
Walking is possible within hours. A supportive bra helps healing.
Weeks 1–2
Most people return to work and light routines after about 7–10 days.
Sport and heavy lifting are possible again, as advised by your surgeon.
About 2–3 hours under general anaesthesia, usually with one night in hospital.
Can a breast lift be combined with implants?
Yes. If you have lost volume as well, silicone implants can be placed in the same operation.
Will there be scars?
Depending on the technique, the scars run around the areola and vertically down (lollipop) or in an inverted-T pattern. They usually become much less visible over time.
Most people return to light routines after about 7–10 days; sport after about 6 weeks.
Plan your breast lift

An arm lift removes loose skin and fat from the upper arms – often after major weight loss or with age – through an incision on the inner or back of the arm. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
About 1.5–2.5 hours
You have loose skin on your upper arms after weight loss or with age.
Incision and tissue removal
An incision is made on the inner or back of the upper arm, and excess skin and fat are removed.
Tightening and contouring
The supporting tissue underneath is tightened and the contour of the upper arm is shaped.
The incisions are closed with sutures and compression garments are put on. You usually stay in hospital for one night.
Walking is possible within hours. Compression garments support healing.
Heavy lifting and intense upper-body training are possible again, as advised.
About 1.5–2.5 hours under general anaesthesia, usually with one night in hospital.
When can I train again?
Heavy lifting and intense upper-body workouts should wait about 6 weeks.
Will there be a scar?
Yes. An arm lift leaves a line-shaped scar on the inner or back of the upper arm, from the armpit to the elbow, which usually fades over time.
Can an arm lift be combined with liposuction?
Yes, it is often combined with liposuction to remove stubborn fat at the same time.
Plan your arm lift

Breast reduction reduces the size and weight of very large breasts. It can relieve back and neck pain, restricted movement and skin irritation and creates a more balanced silhouette. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
Large breasts cause you physical discomfort, for example back, neck or shoulder pain.
You suffer from skin irritation, a poor posture or have difficulty finding clothes that fit.
You would like breasts in better proportion to your body.
After a detailed consultation about your complaints, wishes and health, the operation takes place under general anaesthesia.
Incisions are made around the areola, vertically down the breast and sometimes along the breast crease. Excess breast tissue, fat and skin are removed.
Reshaping and nipple position
The remaining tissue is shaped and, in most cases, the nipple and areola are moved higher while keeping their connection to nerves and blood supply.
Full recovery; sport and heavy lifting are possible again, as advised.
About 2–4 hours under general anaesthesia, depending on the amount of tissue removed, usually with one night in hospital.
Most people return to light routines after about 7–10 days.
When is full recovery?
Usually after about 6 weeks, when sport and heavy lifting are possible again.
Yes. The scars run around the areola and downwards (anchor or vertical lollipop shape) and usually fade over time.
Can I still breastfeed afterwards?
In many cases yes, as modern techniques preserve milk ducts and glands. It depends on the technique and the amount of tissue removed – ask your surgeon in the consultation.
Plan your breast reduction

Eyelid surgery corrects drooping upper eyelids and bags under the eyes. Upper eyelid surgery is usually done under local anaesthesia, lower eyelid surgery generally under general anaesthesia. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
Local or general
Stitches
Removed after about 7 days
After about 3–5 days
Your upper eyelids droop or you have bags under the eyes.
Drooping upper eyelids may even narrow your field of vision.
Upper eyelids
Removes excess skin from the upper lids; usually under local anaesthesia.
Lower eyelids
Treats bags under the eyes; generally under general anaesthesia.
Consultation and planning
The surgeon discusses your wishes and your medical history and makes a personal surgical plan.
Anaesthesia and incision
Under local or general anaesthesia, small incisions are made in the natural creases of the eyelids.
Removing or repositioning tissue
Excess skin, fat and muscle of the upper and/or lower eyelids are removed or repositioned.
Closure and aftercare
The incisions are closed with fine sutures and tapes; the stitches are removed after about 7 days.
After a pre-operative examination, the operation takes place as planned. Your surgeon tells you whether you can return to your hotel the same day.
Swelling and bruising are normal. Most people resume light routines after 3–5 days.
Day 7
The stitches and tapes are removed by the surgeon after about 7 days.
Most people are back to their normal routine after 1–2 weeks; swelling continues to go down.
About 1–2 hours, depending on whether upper, lower or both eyelids are treated.
When are the stitches removed?
Usually after about 7 days, by your surgeon.
In the natural crease of the upper eyelid and directly under the lash line (or inside) of the lower eyelid.
Plan your eyelid surgery

In a Brazilian Butt Lift, fat is removed by liposuction from areas such as the abdomen or flanks, purified and transferred to the buttocks for more volume and shape. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
About 3–5 hours
For about 6 weeks
You would like more volume and a different shape of the buttocks.
You have enough body fat in other areas for the transfer.
Liposuction and fat harvesting
Fat is removed by liposuction from areas such as the abdomen, flanks or thighs – this also shapes these areas.
Purification and fat transfer
The fat is purified, and healthy fat cells are transferred to specific areas of the buttocks.
The small incisions are closed and a compression garment is put on. You usually stay in hospital for 1–2 nights.
Weeks 1–3
Avoid sitting directly on your buttocks for 2–3 weeks; a special pillow helps when sitting is necessary.
Weeks 1–6
The compression garment is worn for about 6 weeks to reduce swelling and support the new contour.
Months 1–3
Part of the transferred fat is naturally absorbed by the body in the first months; the rest stays.
About 3–5 hours under general anaesthesia, depending on the amount of fat, usually with 1–2 nights in hospital.
Can I sit after a BBL?
Avoid sitting directly on your buttocks for about 2–3 weeks; a special pillow helps when you need to sit.
Does all of the transferred fat stay?
No. Usually about 60–70% of the transferred fat stays; the rest is naturally absorbed by the body during the first 3 months.
Plan your BBL

A facelift reduces visible signs of ageing such as sagging skin and deep folds. Depending on your needs, the surgeon chooses a full, mini, mid-face or temporal lift. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
You have sagging skin or deep folds on the face.
You have realistic expectations, discussed with your surgeon.
Types of facelift
Full facelift
Treats the cheeks, jawline and neck.
Mini facelift
A smaller lift for early signs of sagging.
Mid-face lift
Focuses on the cheek area.
Temporal lift
Lifts the area at the temples and eyebrows.
The surgeon assesses your face, discusses your wishes and chooses the suitable technique – full, mini, mid-face or temporal lift.
Anaesthesia and incisions
Under general anaesthesia, incisions are made in the hairline at the temples and along the natural contours around and behind the ears.
Lifting the deeper layers
The surgeon tightens the deeper layer of the face (SMAS), removes excess fat and lays the skin smoothly over the cheeks, jawline and upper neck.
The incisions are closed carefully and dressed. You usually stay in hospital for 1–2 nights.
Swelling and tightness are normal. 1–2 nights in hospital for the first care.
Week 2
Most people return to work and social activities after about 10–14 days.
Swelling goes down fully and the tissues settle within about 3–6 months.
About 3–5 hours under general anaesthesia, depending on the technique, with 1–2 nights in hospital.
When can I go out again?
In the hairline at the temples and along the natural contours around and behind the ears.
Can a facelift be combined with other procedures?
Yes, for example with a neck lift or eyelid surgery – your surgeon advises you.
Plan your facelift

Buccal fat removal reduces the fat pads in the lower cheeks through small incisions inside the mouth, for more sculpted cheeks and a defined jawline. It is usually performed under local anaesthesia. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
Local anaesthesia
About 30–45 minutes
Often the next day
Healing
About 7–10 days
You have naturally round, full cheeks and would like a more defined face.
After a detailed consultation about your wishes and your health, the procedure takes place under local anaesthesia.
Incision and fat removal
Through small incisions inside the cheeks, part of the buccal fat pads is removed – there are no incisions on the face.
Contouring and symmetry
The surrounding tissue is checked so that both sides are even and the cheekbones and jawline stand out.
The incisions are closed with dissolving stitches. You can usually return to your hotel on the same day.
After a pre-operative examination, the operation takes place as planned. Your surgeon tells you when you can return to your hotel – usually on the same day.
Swelling is normal. Many people return to work and social routines the next day.
Days 7–10
The internal stitches dissolve and the tissue heals.
Swelling goes down over the following weeks and the cheek contour settles.
How long does it take?
About 30–45 minutes under local anaesthesia.
Are there visible scars?
No. The incisions are inside the mouth and close with dissolving stitches.
Plan your buccal fat removal

A neck lift tightens loose skin and reshapes the neck and jawline, for example with jowls, a double chin or neck bands. It is often combined with a facelift. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
You have loose neck skin, jowls, a double chin or visible neck bands from ageing or weight loss.
Incision and tissue adjustment
Incisions are made behind the ears and under the chin; excess skin and fat are removed and the neck muscle (platysma) is tightened.
Redraping the skin
The remaining skin is laid smoothly over the new contour of the neck and jawline.
The incisions are closed and a supportive garment is put on. You usually stay in hospital for one night.
A supportive garment helps healing. One night in hospital.
Most people return to work and light routines after about 10–14 days.
Swelling and tightness go down completely within about 1–3 months.
Can it be combined with other procedures?
Yes, a neck lift is often combined with a facelift or with liposuction of the chin area.
Behind the ears, in the hairline and under the chin.
Plan your neck lift

Otoplasty reshapes or repositions prominent or asymmetric ears. It is possible for adults and for children from about 5–6 years of age, once the ears have finished growing. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
Local (adults), general (children)
About 1–1.5 hours
Headband
For about 1–2 weeks
Your ears – or your child’s ears – stick out or are asymmetric.
Adults and children from about 5–6 years of age, once the ears have finished growing.
Good general health.
The surgeon examines the ears, discusses your wishes and plans the correction – for adults and for children from about 5–6 years.
Adults usually receive local anaesthesia, children general anaesthesia.
Reshaping the cartilage
Through an incision in the natural crease behind the ear, the cartilage is reshaped and the ear is set closer to the head with internal sutures.
The incision is closed and a protective headband is put on; it is worn for about 1–2 weeks.
After a pre-operative examination, the operation takes place as planned. Your surgeon tells you when you can return to your hotel.
A protective headband is worn; mild swelling is normal.
Days 3–5
Most people return to work, school and daily activities after about 3–5 days.
The supportive headband is recommended for about 1–2 weeks to protect the new shape.
From what age is otoplasty possible?
For adults and for children from about 5–6 years of age, once the ears have finished growing.
About 1–1.5 hours – under local anaesthesia for adults, general anaesthesia for children.
Where is the incision?
In the natural crease behind the ear.
Plan your ear correction

A beard or moustache transplant gives a fuller, more defined beard or moustache. Follicles, usually from the back of the head, are transplanted into sparse or hairless areas of the face with the FUE or DHI technique, following the natural direction of growth. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
After a few days
First trim
With scissors after 1 month
After 9–12 months
Your beard or moustache grows patchy, thin or unevenly.
You have lost facial hair due to genetics, scars or an injury.
You have enough healthy donor hair.
Beard transplant
For cheeks, jawline and chin – density and design are planned with you.
Moustache transplant
For the upper lip, symmetrical and in the natural direction of growth.
How the procedure works
After a detailed consultation about your wishes and the design, the procedure takes place under local anaesthesia.
Follicle harvesting
Follicles are taken from the donor area at the back of the head with the FUE or DHI technique.
Implantation and design
The follicles are implanted into the beard or moustache area in the natural direction of growth; density and shape are planned with you.
The donor area is cared for and you receive detailed aftercare instructions.
Arrival and procedure
After an examination, the procedure takes place as planned. You return to your hotel on the same day.
Redness and slight swelling go down; most people are back to their routines within a week.
The transplanted hairs fall out temporarily (“shock loss”); the roots stay in place.
Months 3–12
New growth starts around month 3, visible density at about 6 months, and the final result after 9–12 months.
The donor area and the face are numbed with local anaesthesia. Minor tightness afterwards is treated with common painkillers.
When can I shave?
A first light trim with scissors after 1 month; razors or clippers should wait 3–6 months.
Why do the hairs fall out after the transplant?
Between weeks 2 and 4 the transplanted hair shafts fall out temporarily. The roots stay in the skin and grow new hair.
Plan your beard or moustache transplant
FUE Hair Transplant

In an FUE hair transplant, individual hair follicles are taken one by one from the donor area – usually the back or sides of the head – with a fine micro-punch and implanted into thinning or bald areas. No linear incision and no stitches are needed. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
Duration
About 6–8 hours
Back to work
After about 2–3 days
After 12–18 months
You have male pattern baldness, thinning hair or a receding hairline.
You have enough healthy donor hair at the back or sides of the head.
Your hair loss has stabilised.
The surgeon discusses your wishes, examines your hair and scalp and plans the hairline. Local anaesthesia is applied on the day of the procedure.
Follicle extraction
With fine micro-punches, individual follicles are taken from the donor area at the back or sides of the head, where hair is most resistant to hair loss.
Implantation
The follicles are implanted into the thinning or bald areas, following your natural direction of growth.
FUE needs no stitches. You receive personal aftercare instructions, for example on how to wash your hair.
Light activities after 1–2 days; most people return to work after about 2–3 days. Strenuous exercise should wait at least one month.
The transplanted hairs fall out temporarily (“shock loss”) – a normal part of healing; the roots stay in place.
Months 3–18
New hair grows from about month 3, density increases noticeably by month 6, and the final result shows after 12–18 months.
Is an FUE hair transplant painful?
The donor and recipient areas are numbed with local anaesthesia before the procedure. Mild discomfort afterwards is treated with common painkillers.
FUE needs no linear incision and no stitches. The tiny, dot-like marks in the donor area are usually hard to see once healed.
Why does the hair fall out after the transplant?
In the first weeks the transplanted hairs fall out temporarily (“shock loss”). The roots stay in the skin and grow new hair from about month 3.
When can I do sport again?
Light activities are possible after a few days; strenuous exercise and heavy lifting should wait at least one month.
Plan your FUE hair transplant
DHI Hair Transplant

DHI (Direct Hair Implantation) is a further development of FUE: the follicles are taken individually and implanted directly with a special implanter pen (Choi pen), without opening channels in advance. This gives precise control over the depth, angle and direction of each hair – and DHI is also possible without shaving the head. MedLuxLife arranges your online consultation with the surgeon in Istanbul and organises your stay.
After about 2 days
After about 12 months
You have thinning hair, a receding hairline or bald patches.
You would like to keep your hair long – DHI is also possible without shaving.
Classic DHI
Follicles are implanted directly with the Choi pen for a dense, natural hairline.
Unshaven DHI
The recipient area does not have to be shaved – practical for women and for long hair.
The surgeon discusses your wishes and examines your scalp. On the day of the procedure you receive local anaesthesia.
Individual follicles are taken from the donor area at the back or sides of the head.
Direct implantation
The follicles are loaded into the Choi pen and placed directly into the recipient area, with precise control of depth, angle and direction.
DHI needs no stitches. You are monitored briefly and receive personal aftercare instructions.
Days 1–2
Most people return to light routines and to work after about 2 days.
Small scabs and redness go away.
The implanted hairs shed in the first weeks; new hair grows from about month 3–4, and the full result shows after about 12 months.
